newsitem.title: USA: Celgene submits attention deficit drug IND.
newsitem.headline: Celgene submits attention deficit drug IND.

text.p: Celgene Corp said Monday it submitted an investigational new drug application to the Health Protection Branch of Canada to test a drug treating attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children.
The company said it was seeking to start a phase I/II trial for the drug, which is the single isomer version of dl-methylphenidate, the product under the trade name Ritalin.
The company has already submitted an IND with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to initiate Phase I/II clinical trials in the United States.
The company said it hopes the trials will evaluate the potential benefits of d-MPH, including reduced dosage, improved efficacy and reduced side-effects.
It says total U.S. sales in 1996 for dl-methylphenidate were estimated at $300 million.
